memory_safety.feedback: Detected runtime/sanitizer issues in 3/3 test runs. A clean run is not proof of memory safety.

readability.feedback: Readability score is a deterministic heuristic, not an LLM judgment or proof of code quality.

usefulness.example: Apply one test suite and rubric to hundreds of submissions.
usefulness.benefit: Consistent, repeatable grading and faster feedback.

usefulness.example: Show an input that causes a wrong answer with expected and actual output.
usefulness.benefit: Students can reproduce and debug failures.

usefulness.example: Report warning, structure, modularity and readability indicators.
usefulness.benefit: Instructor can assess more than output correctness.

usefulness.example: Flag submissions above a configurable source similarity threshold.
usefulness.benefit: Focus human review on candidate pairs; does not prove copying.

limitations.limitation: Finite tests do not prove correctness
limitations.example: A program passes supplied tests but fails an untested extreme input.
An invalid access exists in a branch none of the supplied inputs reach.

limitations.limitation: Similarity can have false positives and negatives
limitations.example: A short mandated solution looks similar, or copied code is heavily refactored.

limitations.limitation: Heuristic source analyzers can misestimate properties
limitations.example: A loop bound depends on input in a way the lexical estimator does not recognize.

limitations: POSIX resource limits are not a complete security sandbox; use a disposable lab container/VM for untrusted code.
Sanitizers detect only errors triggered by supplied test inputs.
Complexity, structure, readability and similarity are heuristic.
A similarity flag is not proof of plagiarism or LLM use.
